entries.raw: The LLM examined the following data patterns: 1. Mood, Stress, Productivity: Mood and productivity are higher, and stress lower, on days with more sleep, higher steps, and more social contacts (Days 4 and 7). Conversely, mood and productivity drop when sleep is short, steps are low, and stress rises (Days 2–3, 6).
entries.title: The LLM examined the following data patterns: 1. Mood, Stress, Productivity: Mood and productivity are higher, and stress lower, on days with more sleep, higher steps, and more social contacts

rec.title: Figure 2-10. Productivity varies widely with participation higher in more productive cities

entries.raw: 2. Activity & Sedentary Time: Days with fewer than 5,000 steps and long sedentary hours (10–11 h) correspond to lower mood and productivity.
entries.title: Sedentary Time: Days with fewer than 5,000 steps and long sedentary hours (10–11 h) correspond to lower mood and productivity

rec.title: How does relative time in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity correspond to the 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour?
rec.container: Journal of Activity, Sedentary and Sleep Behaviors

entries.raw: 3. Sleep: Better days (4 and 7) align with 7.8–7.9 hours of sleep. Short sleep (5.9–6.2 h) is linked with worse stress and productivity.
entries.title: Sleep: Better days (4 and 7) align with 7.8–7.9 hours of sleep. Short sleep (5.9–6.2 h) is linked with worse stress and productivity

rec.title: Poor sleep quality is associated with worse self-rated health in long sleep duration but not short sleep duration

entries.raw: 4. HRV: HRV is higher (45–46 ms) on good days, and lower (34–36 ms) on stressful, less active days.
entries.title: HRV is higher (45–46 ms) on good days, and lower (34–36 ms) on stressful, less active days

rec.title: 1000 Days of HRV: A Case Study of Daily Post-Wake-Up Heart Rate Variability for Tracking Stressful Life Events

entries.raw: 5. Social Contacts: More interactions (3–4 contacts) coincide with better mood and productivity.
entries.title: Social Contacts: More interactions (3–4 contacts) coincide with better mood and productivity

rec.title: Measuring Contacts and Interactions in Social Networks
